#5401. AFLW ladder with one round to play; ‘Difficult decision’: Dons sack inaugural coach

Essendon will replace inaugural AFLW coach Natalie Wood next season after informing her that her contract would not be renewed for 2027 after the team’s 1-10 record this season.

Wood was informed on Tuesday about the decision, but players were only told after Sunday’s five-point loss to Hawthorn.

Wood is still planning to coach the final round game next Sunday against fellow strugglers Collingwood.

The Dons will be the third AFLW club seeking a coach, joining St Kilda and expansion club Tasmania Devils.

“The club is not offering me a contract as of next year,” Wood said post game on Sunday.

“It’s been a topic of conversation and a lot of questions with our poor performances this year

“It’s a disappointing end, as clearly I would have liked, like the last couple of years, to have better performances on the field.”

The Dons have struggled with injuries and form this season, but Wood was heartened by the club locking in several future leaders to new contracts but they will look for a new coach.

“We have fallen short of what we wanted on field. We believe a change is the right step,” Essendon chief executive Tim Roberts said.

“Natalie has handled this with real integrity, and her commitment to coaching out the season says a lot about her and how much she cares about the players.

“We thank Natalie for everything she has given the club over five seasons, and we wish her all the best for the next step in her football journey.”

Wood was the first female coach to reach 50 games while leading the team for five seasons since they entered the competition.

“[I] just continued on with the week as normal,” Wood said.

“We had two amazing players in Alex Morcom and Maddi Gay having their 50th and 75th game today, so really important celebrations, and we also had Amelia Radford announce her retirement.

“I would prefer no one ever knows, and I’d just disappear off into the sunset without any discussion or interview, but I was particularly aware this week of not wanting to get in the way of those three players.

“We really wanted to beat Hawthorn today. I thought we put up a really good fight, it was an ugly game of footy, tricky conditions. But always forefront of my mind is playing group first – so I thought it was best to hold off until today.

“Aysha (Ward, AFLW general manager) is heavily pregnant and is going on leave in two or three weeks, so I think the club is keen on getting a start in searching for their new coach.”

Wood said it was hard leading the AFLW side while Essendon as a club has faced so many leadership changes in recent seasons.

“Am I disappointed it’s fallen out this way? It depends how narrow of a view I have of it. Sometimes,” Wood said.

“I remember in my job interview, we were discussing about the wants of the role. [At the time], no female coach had lasted longer than two years, and I was not wanting to step into a senior coaching role without being well prepared and supported to have a career that’s longer than two years,” Wood said.

“To be the first female coach to coach 50 games, I’m really proud of that. To build a team from ground-up, as one of the last expansion teams and the season coming forward, it was a mad rush.

“At the same time, the club’s had a lot of instability. There’s been four CEOs, three presidents, three men’s senior captains and three senior coaches, so to build a culture within a program while the instability of the club – and it’s in a good spot now – it’s been hard at times while there’s been so much change in structure and leadership.

“When I look back to the start of the season and we had so many players sign long-term contracts, players who are really important to the program going forward - we’ve built a culture and place where players really want to be. I’ve done something right.”

The Hawks scored a vital win in their quest to make the top eight, winning by five points in rain-soaked conditions at the club’s new base in Dingley.

The Bombers were brave but couldn’t find the last goal they needed to get the win.

Two-time reigning AFLW premiers North Melbourne have fought past a stern challenge from Adelaide to win by nine points and return to the top of the ladder.

The Crows conceded the first two goals in scrappy, wet conditions at North Hobart Oval but kept North goalless in the second term, then kicked two majors to lead by three at halftime.

Adelaide were up by a point at the final change but couldn’t hold on as North overran the Crows late to win 5.8 (38) to 4.5 (29).

Kangaroos stars Jasmine Garner and Ash Riddell had 32 disposals apiece, while Erika O’Shea had 26 and 16 intercepts.

Crows Ebony Marinoff (30 disposals) and Chloe Bown (22) were busy and Christina Leuzzi kicked two goals.

Essendon will replace inaugural AFLW coach Natalie Wood next season after informing her that her contract would not be renewed for 2027 after the team’s 1-10 record this season.

Wood was informed on Tuesday about the decision, but players were only told after Sunday’s five-point loss to Hawthorn.

Wood is still planning to coach the final round game next Sunday against fellow strugglers Collingwood.

The Dons will be the third AFLW club seeking a coach, joining St Kilda and expansion club Tasmania Devils.

Five-goal Sydney star Chloe Molloy has exploded against West Coast to deliver a 22-point victory that seals a finals berth and keeps the Swans in touch with the top four.

Molloy’s terrific bag of five, including three final-term majors, proved the difference at Henson Park as Colin O’Riordan’s Sydney prevailed 12.6 (78) to 8.8 (56).

“Colin challenged us at the start of the week to seize the moment,” Molloy told Fox Footy.

“Sometimes you can shy away from the bigger moments and an opportunity to lock in the finals.

Gold Coast coach Rhyce Shaw was surprised and frustrated at the circumstances around Dekota Baron’s removal from their narrow AFLW win over Richmond.

But Shaw was also adamant that player welfare must come first.

Baron, a Rising Star nominee this season, was floored by a nasty collision with Tigers opponent Montana McKinnon in the first quarter of Saturday’s match on the Gold Coast.

Baron’s head cannoned into McKinnon’s hip. After initially being cleared by doctors to keep playing, the ARC (AFL review centre) intervened and ruled that she needed a head injury assessment.

Melbourne are closing on a AFLW top-four berth after grinding their way to a massive win over the Western Bulldogs on Saturday night.

In wet conditions which hit Victoria hard this weekend – there were fears the game might be delayed because of lightning – the Demons beat the Bulldogs 5.7 (37) to 2.8 (20) at Whitten Oval.

Melbourne are third ahead of next weekend’s trip to Adelaide, while Gold Coast’s narrow win earlier on Saturday meant the Bulldogs dropped to fifth.

The Bulldogs now have another big game on Friday night in Geelong against the Cats, who are on a 10-game winning streak. Star Bulldog Isabelle Pritchard also finished Saturday’s game on the bench with a knee injury.

The Bulldogs did not kick a goal from 15 minutes into the first term until seven minutes into the last.

Geelong have secured an AFLW qualifying final at “our house” with a 30-point win that also put a massive hole in Fremantle’s top-eight hopes.

There could be major injury ramifications out of Saturday’s physical clash at GMHBA Stadium, which the Cats won 9.10 (64) to 5.4 (34).

A heavy collision early in the last quarter put Geelong’s Rachel Kearns out of the game, while Fremantle player Noa McNaughton needed help from two trainers when she also went off in the final term with an ankle injury.

Geelong forward Chantal Mason suffered an ugly cut to her face in a marking contest. Fremantle’s Aoife Healy, Aisling McCarthy and Kiara Bowers, plus Cats player Aishling Moloney all needed injury treatment during the game.

Brisbane had successive wins for the first time in their tough season, mauling home side St Kilda by 52 points at RSEA Park on Saturday.

The Lions’ 11.9 (75) to 3.5 (23) win ended a tough few days for the Saints under interim coach Matt Brewer.

He dropped Jesse Tawhiao-Wardlaw and Maya Louvel-Finn for not meeting team standards.

Tyanna Smith’s second goal reduced the margin to 13 points at halftime and the Saints looked a chance. But they only managed two behinds in the second half as the Lions took control.

#5402. Психолог предупредила о последствиях жизни по принципу «на том свете выспимся»

Психолог Розер Горт предупредила, что жизнь по принципу «на том свете выспимся» — его она раньше придерживалась и сама — может привести к негативным последствиям для организма. Ее слова передает издание Men's Health.

Горт подчеркнула, что из-за недосыпа на первых порах проблемы возникают не со здоровьем, а с темпераментом. К примеру, человек может стать нетерпеливым, импульсивным и склонным к негативным эмоциям, отметила специалистка.

Кроме того, у него зачастую снижается способность запоминать информацию, поэтому закономерно возникают проблемы с учебой и работой, добавила психолог. «Ваша работоспособность падает гораздо быстрее, чем вы это воспринимаете. Вы все еще считаете себя способным на что-то. Это тот же механизм, что и у человека, который выпил алкоголь и чувствует себя совершенно способным сесть за руль», — объяснила она.

Ранее сомнолог Николай Ильин рассказал, какие напитки приводят к бессоннице. Он посоветовал воздержаться от употребления алкоголя в вечернее время.

#5403. Woman who helped dispose of 4-year-old Megan Khung's body, conspired to abuse her pleads guilty

Megan Khung was abused for over a year by her mother and her mother's boyfriend before she died as a result of a punch to the stomach.

A photo of Nouvelle Chua Ruoshi arriving at the Supreme Court on Oct 26, 2026 (left), and a file photo of Megan Khung, who died in February 2020. (Photos: CNA/Lim Li Ting, Instagram/@simonboyyyyyyy)

SINGAPORE: A woman who helped dispose of four-year-old Megan Khung's body and was part of the conspiracy to abuse her pleaded guilty on Monday (Oct 26).

Megan had been abused by her mother, Foo Li Ping, and her mother's boyfriend, Wong Shi Xiang, for over a year before she died as a result of a punch to her stomach.

After Megan's death, Foo and Wong disposed of her body with the help of their friend, Nouvelle Chua Ruoshi.

Chua pleaded guilty on Monday to charges that included conspiracy to commit child abuse, disposal of a corpse and drug consumption.

As part of court proceedings, video clips of the abuse, some filmed by Chua, were played in court. The judge told those in the courtroom that the clips were distressing, asking those who wished to leave to do so.

Megan was born to Foo and Foo's then husband, Khung Wei Nan or Simonboy as he is known online, in October 2015.

Foo and Khung's marriage broke down, and Foo took Megan back to live with Foo's mother.

Foo began dating Wong in late 2018 and moved to live with him from January 2019, with Megan staying over on some weekends.

Sometime in 2019, Chua came to know Foo, and they became close friends, with Chua staying over at Foo's flat with her daughter.

Megan was abused by Foo and Wong when she stayed at the flat from February 2019.

She was caned when she urinated on furniture, leaving bruises, slapped, pushed and punched, forced to wear a soiled diaper over her head and made to eat food from a dustbin.

In a video clip taken by Chua, Megan cried as her mother forced her to wear the soiled diaper on her head, whimpering: "I don't want to wear"

After Foo placed the soiled diaper on Megan's head, covering her face and nose, she slapped her forcefully.

After this, Megan whimpered: "Mommy, I can't see."

In another clip, Megan was shown standing at the foot of a block with red marks drawn all over her face. She had been paraded in public after Wong drew on her face, with Chua recording this.

On another occasion, Megan's head was shaved to humiliate her.

Megan was starved from January 2020 to prevent her from defecating around the house. She was not allowed to wear clothes because of the bloodstains left on the fabric by her wounds.

Chua filmed Megan repeatedly asking her mother for permission to wear a shirt in February 2020.

Megan was also made to sleep in a planter box outside the master bedroom which faced the afternoon sun.

Chua told Foo to feed Megan her mucus since she was hungry, and Foo wiped a mucus-stained handkerchief forcefully over Megan's tongue.

On Feb 21, 2020, Megan was deprived of food for the whole day.

Foo and Wong made the child stand in front of them and Wong scolded Megan before punching her in the stomach.

The force of the punch caused Megan's back to hit against the wall with a loud thud.

Chua arrived at the flat in the early hours of Feb 22, 2020, and learnt what happened.

She saw Megan lying on the bedroom floor holding onto her stomach in pain.

Chua told Foo and Wong about this but they dismissed it and said Megan was merely trying to get attention.

Chua then ignored Megan and joined the couple in taking drugs in the living room.

Several hours later, Chua saw Megan in the same position. The group took turns to perform cardiopulmonary resuscitation on Megan.

The group left Megan's body in the flat on Feb 23, 2020 and stayed elsewhere, with the couple discussing how to dispose of her body.

On May 8, 2020, the trio returned to the flat. Wong had wrapped Megan's corpse and placed it in a box, and he retrieved the box with Foo.

Megan's corpse, still in the box, was burnt in a metal barrel at a workshop for several hours.

Wong later swept the ashes inside the barrel into a trash bag and drove to East Coast Park on his own, scattering Megan's ashes into the sea.

Neither the metal barrel nor Megan's remains were ever recovered.

Simonboy lodged a police report concerning the whereabouts of Megan on Jul 20, 2020.

Foo was sentenced in April 2025 to 19 years' jail for charges including allowing the death of a child, child abuse and disposing of a corpse.

Specifically, her sentence for the disposal of a corpse charge was five-and-a-half years' jail.

Wong received 30 years' jail and 17 strokes of the cane in April 2025 for charges including culpable homicide, drug consumption and disposing of Megan's corpse.

His sentence for disposing of a corpse was six years' jail.

The sentencing of Foo and Wong triggered a review of the case by the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF).

A review panel in October 2025 identified serious shortcomings across the agencies responsible for Megan's welfare.

In November 2025, MSF said it would establish a social services coordination centre on top of improving protocols and coordination with the police for missing children.

Chua is represented by Mr Thangavelu, Ms Sugenya Manogaran and Ms Tan Jun Yin from Trident Law.

For intentionally disposing of a corpse, Chua can be jailed for up to seven years.

#5404. 'Classic Canberra idea': architects to compete in 'missing middle' design contest

Canberra's suburbs have long had a copy-and-paste quality about them, with government houses built over and over to pre-approved designs.

Now the ideas of a new generation of architects are being sought for the capital in a national design competition for a pattern book of "missing middle" house designs.

Planning Minister Chris Steel said the government was building on a "classic Canberra idea".

Much of Canberra had been built on pattern housing, when pre-designed homes were used to efficiently grow the capital in the post-war years, he said.

"First, we made it possible to build missing middle homes, now we're fast-tracking new homes through a pattern book approach," Mr Steel said.

"This pattern book will give Canberrans a range of top quality, sustainable, and affordable home designs that can be built without the need for a DA."

But unlike the Department of Works' 400 series designs for houses that gave mid-century Canberra swathes of small three-bedroom homes on big suburban blocks, the government wants innovation on a tighter scale.

The "missing middle" housing the government is working to encourage, sitting between existing detached housing and high-density apartment buildings, includes duplexes, dual-occupancies, townhouses and terraces.

Last week, planning law changes passed the Legislative Assembly to make smaller-scale subdivisions faster to approve, permit secondary residences on single-dwelling leases without a Crown lease variation, and streamline lease variations for minor changes.

The planning minister said the changes would deliver faster approvals for "missing middle" housing projects.

Mr Steel said the pattern book would demonstrate how well-designed "missing middle" housing could enhance Canberra's suburbs.

"It will provide practical examples of housing that responds to our unique climate, landscape and local character, while supporting a more compact and efficient city," he said.

"The competition represents an opportunity to harness the creativity of the design profession in pursuit of a shared goal: delivering more homes without compromising on quality."

ACT government architect Catherine Townsend said the competition would encourage creative and practical approaches to housing design and help shape more diverse, liveable and sustainable neighbourhoods.

"I am very pleased to launch the Expression of Interest for the Canberra House Pattern Book Design Competition, an important initiative to expand housing choice and support thoughtful, sensitive neighbourhood and precinct development," Ms Townsend, a Life Fellow of the Royal Institute of Architects, said.

"The competition seeks innovative, cost-efficient design solutions that respond to the evolving needs of families while reflecting the unique character and environmental context of Canberra, the Bush Capital."

The competition will be a two-stage process. First, expressions of interest will be invited from Australian architects, building designers and architecture students.

Next, about 16 selected professional entrants and about six student entrants will be tasked with submitting house designs, which will be publicly exhibited.

The winners will continue to a post-competition stage to focus on detailed design work and refinement to incorporate the plans in the Canberra House Pattern Book.

The book will serve as a library of pre-qualified housing designs that can be quickly approved for construction, the government said.

Expressions of interest for the design competition shut on December 4.

#5406. 'Can't abstain from this debate': Pacific nations the next frontier in deep-sea mining

SBS acknowledges the Traditional Custodians of Country and their connections and continuous care for the skies, lands and waterways throughout Australia.

Commercial deep-sea mining in the Pacific could begin in months without policy guardrails due to increasing rivalry between the United States and China over critical minerals, a new report warns.

Analysis by the Lowy Institute has found mining could start as early as 2027, with the floor of the Pacific Ocean holding vast quantities of prized resources.

The contest between the world's two biggest economies is being driven by demand created by batteries, weapons systems, and power grids.

The region's nations are split between the promise of economic spoils and the risk of irreversible damage to the ecosystem, fisheries, food security, livelihoods and culture, according to the research.

It argues the absence of an international governance framework for commercial deep-sea mining leaves Pacific states negotiating without internationally agreed protections.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

This also leaves them dependent on individual agreements drafted by companies seeking to mine their ocean floor.

"For the Pacific Island nations caught in the middle of this great power battle for critical mineral supremacy, the economic proposition is difficult to refuse," the Lowy Institute's Connor Graham writes.

"The problem is not that Pacific nations disagree, it is that they are being forced to negotiate individually against parties with vastly more resources, information, and legal capacity, and that the international framework designed to protect them has stalled."

Graham said while Australia was yet to take a clear position on deep-sea mining in the Pacific, it has the standing, relationships, and institutional presence to make an impact.

This includes its membership in the Pacific Islands Forum and as a long-standing ally of the US.

"A commitment to standards that have not been written as a condition for activity that is about to begin is less of a policy, and more of an abstention," he said.

"But Australia cannot afford to abstain from this debate."

Countries including Australia have started to enter into deals for critical minerals, which are crucial for a number for emerging technologies.

The federal government has announced a $1.2 billion critical minerals strategic reserve to secure the supply of key minerals deemed crucial for Australia's economy and national security.

#5408. ''J'ai décidé de subir cette ablation du sein… je n'ai plus rien à prouver à cette féminité'', Dr Fatma Guénoune

En ce début du mois d'octobre, Fatma Guénoune enchaîne les entretiens avec les médias.

Depuis qu'elle est engagée dans la lutte contre le cancer, elle sait qu'''Octobre rose'', cette campagne de sensibilisation contre la maladie, constitue un moment unique pour elle, celles et ceux qui se battent contre ce mal silencieux qui fait des ravages chez les femmes.

Cette année, Octobre rose revêt une signification particulière pour cette femme, médecin à la soixantaine révolue, elle incarne depuis plusieurs décennies la lutte contre le cancer du sein au Sénégal.

En effet, Fatma Guénoune a découvert il y a quelques mois, à la suite d'un banal contrôle, qu'elle avait elle-même une tumeur cancéreuse.

''J'ai découvert ma tumeur par l'auto-examen, l'autopalpation'', déclare Dr Fatma Guénoune. ''Quand j'ai palpé mon sein, j'ai vu une masse qui n'était pas une masse régulière. Du coup, j'ai trouvé que c'était suspect et c'était un cancer'' relate-t-elle ne laissant aucune émotion l'envahir au moment de raconter son histoire.

''Je suis médecin, j'ai l'habitude de palper des seins, de palper des masses. Et quand j'ai palpé mon sein, cette tumeur-là, j'ai su que c'était un cancer'', précise Mme Guénoune, Médecin spécialiste des pathologies cervico-vaginales, engagée dans la lutte contre le cancer depuis plusieurs décennies.

Alors qu'elle consacre tout son engagement et toute son énergie à la lutte contre le cancer, à offrir des services de dépistage gratuits et un accompagnement aux femmes démunies atteintes de cette maladie, Fatma Guénoune doit désormais vivre et affronter la maladie en tant que patiente.

Une épreuve qu'elle a l'habitude de voir d'autres femmes affronter et qu'elle a acceptée personnellement de faire face à son tour en tant que croyante.

''J'ai rendu grâce à Dieu, parce que moi j'ai vécu le cancer dans ma chair, dans ma famille. J'ai accompagné des membres de ma famille vers la mort'' dit-elle.

Loin d'être déboussolée par l'apparition de cette tumeur à ce stade de sa vie, elle soutient n'avoir ''pas été déstabilisée''.

''J'ai l'habitude de dire, c'est docteur Fatma Guénoune qui a diagnostiqué la maladie de Fatma Guénoune et c'est le comportement que j'ai à l'endroit des malades'' explique celle qui dirige la LISCA, (Ligue sénégalaise contre le cancer) depuis plus de dix ans.

Elle déclare que la découverte de cette tumeur cancéreuse a renforcé sa foi. Fatma Guénoune s'estime même plus chanceuse que des milliers d'autres patientes car ''je n'ai pas eu à subir une chimiothérapie, ni une radiothérapie''.

Des informations vérifiées à portée de main

Toutefois, elle a dû prendre une décision radicale en subissant une ablation des seins. ''J'ai pris cette décision parce que le cancer du sein est génétique chez moi. Donc, conserver un sein et où un cancer pourra survenir, ce n'est pas la peine. C'est vivre avec un stress permanent. Pour m'éviter de stresser, de faire un futur un autre cancer du sein, j'ai décidé de subir cette ablation bilatérale''.

''Je l'ai acceptée parce que je pense qu'à mon âge, je n'ai plus rien à prouver à cette féminité'' déclare Fatma Guénoune ajoutant ''n'avoir pas de scrupule à me montrer sans sein''.

Depuis qu'elle a subi cette ablation des seins, elle suit une hormonothérapie, un traitement qui va durer quelques années encore.

Interrogée sur la réaction de ses proches qui l'ont connue dans ce combat contre le cancer et qui doivent désormais la regarder en tant que patiente, Fatma Guénoune précise que ses proches ''ne croyaient pas à mon diagnostic''.

''J'ai un jeune frère qui pensait que je bluffais. C'est lui qui a énormément pleuré quand il m'a vu avec mes pansements parce qu'il n'y croyait pas'' au début.

Poursuivant son récit, elle raconte avoir gardé toute sa sérénité après le diagnostic final, ce qui a poussé beaucoup de personnes à se poser des questions sur sa maladie.

''Ma sœur par exemple, elle me dit pourquoi tu n'as pas pleuré ? Je lui ai dit, si je pleure qui va vous réconforter ? D'habitude c'est moi qui vous réconforte, vous ne pouvez pas me réconforter, donc je suis obligée d'être forte pour moi et pour vous''.

Le fait d'être personnellement affecté par une maladie que l'on combat tous les jours aurait pu changer son regard. Que nenni.

''Mon regard n'a pas changé, au contraire, j'ai toujours soutenu les femmes qui étaient dans le besoin, des femmes malades, des femmes démunies qui ne pouvaient pas se soigner'' rappelle Dr Fatma Guénoune.

Un engagement qu'elle a eu en tant que médecin et qui l'a conduit à faire de la lutte contre le cancer, son cheval de batail et à rejoindre la LISCA qu'elle dirige maintenant depuis plus d'une décennie.

Au sein de cette organisation, elle avec ses camarades de l'association cultive un esprit de solidarité envers toutes les femmes atteintes de cancer face à l'adversité de ce mal.

''Nous croyons qu'ensemble, nous pouvons surmonter les défis et apporter du réconfort à ceux qui en ont le plus besoin. Chaque geste, chaque don, chaque action, qu'elle soit petite ou grande, renforce le tissu solidaire qui soutient ceux qui luttent contre le cancer''

''Le cancer est une maladie redoutable, mais l'espoir est notre moteur. Nous savons que chaque progrès, chaque victoire, chaque recherche menée contribue à un avenir meilleur. Nous croyons qu'avec le soutien de tous, de l'espoir naît la guérison'' indique l'organisation.

Environ 2 220 nouveaux cas et plus de 1 300 décès sont rapportés chaque année au Sénégal, selon les chiffres avancés par la LISCA.

Les malades démunies qui arrivent à la LISCA cherchent une oreille attentive, un accompagnement dans la prise en charge de cette maladie dont les coûts médicaux directs moyens sont estimés à 5,3 millions de FCFA pour le traitement du cancer du sein.

Lorsque le dossier d'une patiente est accepté après une enquête, l'organisation prend en compte les produits de chimiothérapie, les intrants, les analyses, les scanners, l'intervention chirurgicale, la radiothérapie, le suivi post-thérapeutique et assure un soutien psychologique aux patientes.

Face au poids du cancer du sein, la LISCA intensifie ses actions de prévention et mise sur le dépistage précoce qui demeure à ce jour l'arme la plus efficace pour sauver des vies et alléger le fardeau financier qui pèse sur la tête des familles des personnes atteintes de cancer du sein.

Au Sénégal, 70 à 80 % des cas de cancer du sein sont diagnostiqués à un stade avancé, rendant la rémission quasi impossible.

#5409. 'Rockstar' ABC radio producer retires after 38-year career

It's not everyday that Paul Keating calls you during dinner, but for Yusuke Aso it was just Wednesday.

The veteran radio producer will retire after a 38-year career next week, but he hasn't forgotten this one exceptional phone call 20 years ago.

He had teed the former prime minister to speak on 702 ABC Sydney radio about being appointed to a panel in 2006 to design what would become Barangaroo.

Meanwhile, his old federal party had just changed their leader to a relatively unknown Queensland MP, Kevin Rudd.

702 ABC Sydney producer Yusuke Aso and presenter Peter Luck.  (Supplied)

Just as Yusuke was sitting down with his small toddlers, the phone starts ringing. Yusuke recalls the conversation:

"It's Paul Keating here, Yusuke. This Trioli girl, she's not going to ask me about this Labor Party stuff, is she?"

Yusuke says he's not had a night call from a former prime minister since then.

Being an early morning radio producer, he is usually the one doing the calling at odd hours.

Yusuke started his career at the ABC at 2BL when it was based at Forbes Street in Kings Cross. (Supplied)

Over nearly four decades, he's been ringing Sydney's movers and shakers in the early hours to convince them to come on air to discuss the stories of the day.

Through his career at ABC Sydney local radio, even since it used to be known as 2BL, he learned just when he could call anyone for any story regarding the harbour city.

Now after a long career of phone conversations with politicians, sports stars, musicians and academics, Yusuke is hanging up the headphones.

The veteran producer saw the end of using tape for broadcast audio. (Supplied)

Yusuke started his Sydney local radio career with the ABC in 1988 producing Bob Hudson's night-time radio show back when the radio studios were in a basement at Forbes Street in Kings Cross.

He found his way to morning radio in 1990 when producing for the late Andrew Olle, a time he more or less stuck with for 36 years.

He's produced for over a dozen presenters including Phillip Clark, Angela Catterns, Sally Loane, Virginia Trioli, Deborah Cameron, Linda Mottram, Wendy Harmer, Robbie Buck, James Valentine, Cassie McCullagh, Sarah Macdonald and currently Hamish Macdonald.

Yusuke Aso will depart the ABC after 38 years producing radio programs for ABC local radio in Sydney.  (ABC News: Declan Bowring)

Over the years he's built a famously extensive contact book with 40,000 entries. He remembers when he saved too many contacts for his iPhone to handle.

"I didn't know there was a ceiling to be busted, but 25,000 apparently used to be the ceiling maximum that the iPhone's phone app could actually store," Yusuke told 702 ABC Sydney.

702 ABC Sydney Mornings presenter Hamish Macdonald describes him as an "absolute rockstar" whose contact book is like "having the keys to the world of making radio".

Yusuke's contact list has become the stuff of legend among Sydney radio producers. (ABC News: Declan Bowring)

"There is rarely a contact he doesn't have and his joy and enthusiasm for landing the best possible guest is unmatched," Macdonald said.

Macdonald paid tribute to Yusuke as a colleague and friend who was a master of what Yusuke calls "flow radio".

"Rather than just moving through a daily rundown, he wants the listener to feel a sense of flow between all the subjects and pivots so that it feels organic and comfortable," Macdonald said.

This extensive contact book has been a secret weapon of ABC Sydney radio presenters for decades. Angela Catterns, whose breakfast show he produced from 2000–2003, said Yusuke could always "sniff out" the best stories.

"Whenever I presented a radio show with Yusuke producing I know I was in safe hands," Catterns said.

Just about every presenter agrees with Catterns' assessment.

"He's diligent, he's hard-working, he knows where all the bodies are buried," presenter Robbie Buck, who Yusuke worked for between 2018 and 2021, said.

Yusuke first produced radio for ABC Sydney local radio in 1988. (ABC News: Declan Bowring)

Former 2BL station manager Peter Wall remembers hiring Yusuke well before he built his reputation as a story wrangler.

He remembers Yusuke, who had arrived in Australia from Japan in 1985, as a "young Japanese guy who loved Australia".

He remembers at the end of this job interview Yusuke saying the expression "she's apples", although Yusuke recalls saying "good as gold".

Yusuke remembers the big difference in coming to Australia was how it was more open and embracing of women and gay people.

"There was a high percentage of females who weren't wearing uniforms and who weren't just serving cups of tea to male office workers, because that's a corporate environment I've just come from," Yusuke said.

Colleagues said Yusuke was a master of "flow radio". (Supplied)

"I had previously never met so many openly gay male people in my life and that was a genuine eye opener for me."

As well as his deep knowledge for news stories and extensive contacts, Yusuke made himself known for his personal style of vests and love for music.

He intends to continue his occasional translating work, but he's also hoping to spend more time being a different kind of rockstar, at home with his rock music collection, after he puts his last show to air.

"I go away from this place with a pretty profound sense of accomplishment," Yusuke said.

"I never thought I'd be in a place like this, doing things like this. And I feel so humbled and honoured and flattered to have served and played a role in this kind of organisation."

Header image: The veteran producer became well-known around the office for his stylish vests and love of music.  (ABC News: Declan Bowring)

#5411. Tassie, Vic gold output clears Kaiser Reef debt as cash hits $40M

You have reached your maximum number of saved items.

Remove items from your saved list to add more.

You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month.

Dual-asset gold producer Kaiser Reef has wiped a key debt from its books after a solid September quarter, a move expected to unchain about $600,000 a month in operating cash flow.

The company banked 6263 ounces of gold during the period, boosting its cash and bullion balance to a healthy $40 million and allowing it to fully repay the senior secured gold loan used to acquire its flagship Henty gold mine in Tasmania.

Production from the company’s two Australian assets continued to build momentum during the period, with total gold output rising to 6263 ounces from 6000 ounces in the prior quarter. The cornerstone Henty mine churned out 5692 ounces of gold and a further 5259 ounces of silver, while its Maldon project in Victoria chipped in another 572 ounces of gold. Impressively, the Maldon operation has now lifted its output for three consecutive quarters, jumping 65 per cent since March.

Total production generated an underlying cash flow of $5.6 million for the quarter, which more than covered $2.8 million in debt and deferred payments, allowing Kaiser to increase its net cash and bullion position by a hefty $2.8 million.

The strong financial position enabled the company to make a final delivery of 104 ounces of gold in October, wiping the slate clean on the 1872-ounce Auramet gold loan. With that facility retired, Kaiser’s only remaining gold delivery obligation is a deferred payment to Catalyst Metals as part of the Henty acquisition, requiring 50 ounces per month through to October 2030. However, the company says repaying the principal acquisition loan from the mine’s own cash flow is an important milestone.

Kaiser Reef managing director Brad Valiukas said: “Kaiser delivered 6263oz of gold across Henty and Maldon during the quarter, while increasing cash and bullion to A$40 million, paying down debt and advancing Maldon. We have completely repaid the Auramet gold loan, on schedule, with the final delivery made in October. The gold loan helped us acquire Henty, and repaying it from Henty’s own cash flow is an important milestone for Kaiser.”

The impressive quarterly report further underscores a remarkable full-year turnaround for Kaiser, which swung from a $20.24 million statutory loss in FY2025 to a $16.8 million after-tax profit in FY2026, backed by an impressive $44.7 million cash inflow from operations.

The Henty mine, nestled in Tasmania’s richly endowed Mount Read Volcanics belt alongside the legendary Rosebery and Mount Lyell operations, remains the company’s gold-producing workhorse. A recent resource and reserve update effectively offset mining depletion, maintaining the mine’s ore reserve at 198,000 ounces of gold and its overall resource at 429,000 ounces. In a shrewd move to sweat its assets, the company is also working with fellow ASX-lister Flynn Gold to process its ore through Henty’s 300,000-tonne-per-annum processing plant. As part of the expansion plan, Kaiser has applied to increase its tailings capacity by two million tonnes.

While Henty provides the cash flow, Kaiser’s Maldon operation in Victoria’s fabled Golden Triangle offers a significant high-grade growth opportunity. The project, with a strong track record of producing 1.75 million ounces at a staggering 28 grams per tonne (g/t) gold, is anchored by the fully permitted 200,000-tonne-per-annum Porcupine Flats processing facility. Its Union Hill deposit hosts an inferred resource of 187,000 ounces grading a solid 4.44g/t gold, with site stockpiles adding a further 11,700 ounces.

All up, the company’s global resource stands at 5.53 million tonnes grading 3.46g/t gold for 615,000 ounces. With FY27 total production targeted at around 32,000 ounces and no hedging in place, the gold producer appears well positioned to capture more upside should the bullion price remain steady.

Another major milestone for the quarter was the start of underground development at the Union Hill mine. The new development will provide access for underground diamond drilling to test the northern extensions of existing workings at Maldon’s Eaglehawk, Linscott’s, Ladies and Sailors Reefs targets.

The underground push adds another dimension to a busy surface exploration campaign aimed at building a pipeline of fresh drill targets. Recent infill soil sampling has outlined strong, continuous gold and arsenic anomalies across multiple structures, with some promising trends extending over 1.5 kilometres of strike. This work has been bolstered by a helicopter-borne magnetic and radiometric survey, providing a clearer picture of the structural architecture, with a surface diamond drilling campaign also ongoing.

With the Henty operation humming along and paying the bills, Kaiser appears to be in an enviable position of being largely debt-free and sitting on a sizeable cash pile as it methodically advances exploration across one of Victoria’s most celebrated high-grade goldfields. With no hedging in place and a production target of 32,000 ounces for FY27, the company looks to be fully exposed to any upside in the gold price. As drill rods turn on both surface and underground hotspots at Maldon, punters will likely be watching closely for the results to start flowing.

#5412. Моющая в бикини лошадь «ангел» Victoria's Secret восхитила пользователей сети

Южноафриканская супермодель Кэндис Свейнпол, известная как один из «ангелов» бренда Victoria’s Secret, в откровенном образе помыла лошадь. Кадры опубликованы на ее странице в Instagram (принадлежит компании Meta, признанной экстремистской организацией и запрещенной в РФ).

38-летняя манекенщица была запечатлена в бикини с принтом, высоких белых носках и черных сапогах. Она распустила вьющиеся светлые волосы и надела серьги необычной формы. При этом знаменитость поливала животное водой из шланга.

Пользователи сети восхитились внешним видом звезды в комментариях под постом. «Очень красивая», «Вау», «Невероятная», «Покупаю такие же наряды, чтобы походить на вас!» — впечатлились они.

В мае Свейнпол топлес послушала музыку и восхитила фанатов. Модель снялась перед камерой, сидя на столе в одних трусах от бикини.

#5413. Former Berry staffer seeks declaration conduct was not corrupt

The former ministerial chief of staff at the centre of a major Integrity Commission investigation has taken the watchdog to court, seeking a declaration his conduct was not corrupt.

Joshua Ceramidas has launched Federal Court action against the commission, arguing the findings of serious corrupt conduct in the handling of a primary school upgrade contract were not supported by evidence.

An amended originating application filed on behalf of Mr Ceramidas alleged the findings were affected by jurisdictional error because they were not supported by the evidence and were also irrational, illogical or unreasonable.

The commission's findings that Mr Ceramidas acted at the behest of or in the interests of the Construction, Forestry and Maritime Employees Union's (CFMEU) ACT branch, that he had a "close relationship with the union" and strongly backed the union's position and intended to help it succeed were among those Mr Ceramidas' claim said were not supported by evidence.

The claim also argued the Integrity Commission's finding Mr Ceramidas' actions constituted a criminal offence was wrong because the commission misconstrued or misunderstood elements of the offence and asked itself the wrong questions.

Mr Ceramidas was deputy chief minister Yvette Berry's chief of staff at the time the commission found he and the head of the Education Directorate, Katy Haire, "dishonestly provided a back door by which the strategic interests of the CFMEU were given priority" in the way a contract was awarded for a primary school upgrade.

Mr Ceramidas "acted in his own interest for the purpose of currying favour with the CFMEU", did not disclose his actions to Ms Berry and lied to the territory's corruption watchdog, the Operation Kingfisher report said.

Mr Ceramidas wants the court to declare the corruption findings were affected by jurisdictional errors and his conduct did not amount to corrupt conduct or serious corrupt conduct.

The case was listed for mention on October 16.

The acting head of the ACT public service, Russ Campbell, on Wednesday confirmed Mr Ceramidas was no longer a territory employee.

"It is not appropriate to comment further because of pending legal proceedings relating to his employment," Mr Campbell said in a statement.

"The territory is not funding any legal costs for Mr Ceramidas' challenge to the Integrity Commission's report."

Attorney-General Tara Cheyne last week told the Legislative Assembly she had received a request to intervene in the Federal Court matter but had declined.

The commission released its long-awaited Operation Kingfisher report in July, having also found the former head of the Education Directorate, Katy Haire, had engaged in serious corrupt conduct.

"Not only was the process itself improperly skewed, resulting in manifest unfairness and also, as it happened, substantially increased cost, but both Ms Haire and Mr Ceramidas undertook a calculated attempt to cover up the truth of what occurred," the report said.

"Accordingly, the corrupt conduct of each amounted to serious corrupt conduct."

Ms Haire resigned from her post as the director-general of the Education Directorate in 2024.

While the corruption watchdog cannot rule whether corruption amounts to a criminal offence, Integrity Commissioner Michael Adams KC's report noted Mr Ceramidas' actions could constitute the offences of abusing public office and conspiracy to defraud.

The findings prompted Yvette Berry, whom Mr Ceramidas worked for from 2016 before joining the ACT public service, to resign from cabinet. No findings were made against Ms Berry.

#5415. Indonesia strengthens measures against stock manipulation after market rout triggered by MSCI

Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto told his Cabinet last week that MSCI was trying to "intimidate" Indonesia, but said the country would not be afraid.

Workers walk past an electronic board displaying stock movement at the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) in Jakarta, Indonesia on Oct 16, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Ajeng Dinar Ulfiana)

JAKARTA: Indonesia on Monday (Oct 26) introduced more measures to address stock market manipulation, including adding independent parties to a committee determining stocks with concentrated ownership structures, after MSCI said the country could be demoted due to concerns about opaque trading.

The measures came after MSCI announced earlier this month that it could demote Indonesia's stock exchange to "standalone" market status, saying not enough had been done to arrest coordinated trading practices in its stock market.

That was more severe than the global index provider's January warning that it could downgrade the country to "frontier" status. At present, MSCI still classifies Indonesia as an "emerging" market.

The Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) plans to expand the membership of a committee that comes up with a list of stocks with high shareholder concentration to include independent parties like Indonesian academics and F Chapman Taylor as a representative of foreign investors, chief Jeffrey Hendrik said at a press conference.

Previously, the committee members were officials from capital market authorities. Taylor is a former partner with investment company the Capital Group and is currently an adviser to Indonesia's sovereign wealth fund, Danantara.

"We encourage the IDX to strengthen the mechanism and methodology of trading supervision, including its capacity to identify patterns of irregular transactions, detect coordinated trading and strengthen the mechanism to respond to such events," said Hasan Fawzi, the financial regulator's capital market supervisor.

Last week, the IDX said it would exclude stocks with high shareholding concentrations from its main Jakarta index starting on Nov 2. The current list includes 80 companies.

The MSCI downgrade warning spurred Indonesia's deepest-ever two-day stock selloff on Oct 16 and Oct 19, sending the main index to its lowest point since 2020. It has since rebounded.

At 1.15pm Singapore time on Monday, the index was down around 1 per cent.

The exchange also plans to launch investigations when it detects possible coordinated trading to manipulate share prices and freeze suspicious investor accounts, Hendrik said.

The new measure, to take effect in November, is more proactive than the IDX's previous response. The IDX previously warned public investors of unusual market activities when a stock price moved sharply and requested an explanation from the company. The process could also lead to a temporary freeze in share trading.

A policy that allows share buybacks without requiring approval from a general shareholders' meeting has also been extended until June 2027, Hasan said, adding that any buyback must consider rules about the minimum free float, or shares available to trade in the market.

Hasan said Indonesia has been communicating with MSCI and other global index providers like FTSE Russell to reiterate its regulators' commitment to market reforms.

The market showed resilience following MSCI's recent announcement, Hasan said, describing local investors as "mature" and "wise" for buying stocks in companies with good fundamentals.

President Prabowo Subianto told his Cabinet last week that MSCI was trying to "intimidate" Indonesia, but said the country would not be afraid, striking a combative tone in his first public reaction to the downgrade warning.

Since MSCI's January warning, Indonesia has launched a series of reforms including releasing more details on investor accounts and ownership data, increasing the minimum free-float level and unveiling record fines against parties involved in market manipulation.

#5416. 'Second chance at life': Sydney woman speaks publicly after surviving shark attack

SBS acknowledges the Traditional Custodians of Country and their connections and continuous care for the skies, lands and waterways throughout Australia.

A Sydney mother has spoken publicly for the first time since surviving a shark attack more than two months ago, crediting community support with helping her "get better, not bitter".

In a post on her GoFundMe donation page, Leah Stewart, 34, said she still had a long way to go, but her recovery had been "remarkable".

"A huge part of that is because of the absolute army of love, support, prayers and encouragement surrounding my family and I from all over the world," she said.

"That means more to me than I can say, and I truly believe it’s played a huge role in my recovery."

Stewart was swimming between the flags close to shore when she was attacked by a great white shark at Coogee Beach on 13 June.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

She was rushed to hospital in a critical condition, being induced in a coma and undergoing multiple surgeries, including the amputation of one of her arms.

The mother of one said she had been focused on her recovery and had "progressed enough to build some independence, and I can finally see some light after all of this".

"I want you to know that I feel like I’ve been given a second chance at life, and I’m not going to waste it. As I get better, I know I’ll make something of this second chance and aim to give back even more in generosity, care, and love. I will forever be grateful for everything, and everyone, I’ve been given," she said.

"You've inspired me to get better, not bitter."

Stewart thanked those who had contributed to the fundraiser, which had reached more than $558,000, but it was time to turn donations off.

"What you’ve offered has given us enough to recover, to stay in our home, and to give us options for further medical treatment down the road," she said.

Sydney has experienced a spate of shark attacks this year, including three in just 48 hours in January.

On 18 January, 12-year-old Nico Antic was critically injured and later died after being attacked by a suspected bull shark while swimming off rocks in Vaucluse in Sydney Harbour.

The following day, Andre de Ruyter, 27, was attacked while surfing near Manly, suffering extreme blood loss and undergoing surgery to have one of his legs amputated.

An 11-year-old boy's surfboard was also bitten at Dee Why Beach on the same day, but the young surfer escaped injury.

After Stewart was attacked in June, NSW Premier Chris Minns said his government would invest an extra $34 million in drone coverage across NSW beaches.

#5420. Des voitures incendiées et des magasins pillés : des violences anti-migrants éclatent en Afrique du Sud

Au moins 24 véhicules ont été incendiés et des magasins appartenant à des étrangers pillés en Afrique du Sud, alors que des manifestations anti-immigration ont dégénéré en violences dans deux grandes villes, selon la police.

Des affrontements ont éclaté jeudi à Soweto, une vaste agglomération située à l'extérieur de Johannesburg, la plus grande ville du pays, et à Durban, un important port de la côte est.

Ces violences surviennent dans un contexte de colère croissante suite à une décision de justice obligeant le gouvernement à lever les obstacles qui empêchaient certains migrants de demander l'asile.

L’Afrique du Sud a connu des flambées répétées de violence xénophobe, ciblant souvent les migrants des pays voisins.

La manifestation de jeudi a dégénéré en violence suite à des allégations selon lesquelles un ressortissant étranger aurait agressé un manifestant à Durban.

Trois ressortissants étrangers ont été arrêtés dans le cadre de cette agression présumée, a indiqué la police.

À Durban, dans la province orientale du KwaZulu-Natal, des manifestants se sont rassemblés devant un centre d'accueil de réfugiés géré par le gouvernement pour exiger l'arrêt de l'acceptation des demandes d'asile.

La police a tiré des balles en caoutchouc pour disperser la foule tandis que les commerces du centre-ville fermaient leurs portes.

Des informations vérifiées à portée de main

« Des affrontements ont eu lieu entre des ressortissants étrangers présents dans la région et des citoyens sud-africains », a déclaré Xolani Fihla, un haut responsable de la police locale, à la chaîne de télévision publique SABC.

« Pour le moment, je peux confirmer qu'aucun blessé n'a été signalé », a-t-il ajouté.

La police a indiqué que 14 véhicules avaient été incendiés à Durban et 10 à Soweto, où des coups de feu ont également été signalés lors d'affrontements entre résidents et commerçants étrangers.

Le commissaire national de police par intérim, le lieutenant-général Puleng Dimpane, a condamné la destruction de biens.

À Orlando West, un quartier de Soweto, les habitants s'étaient initialement rassemblés pour exiger la fermeture des petites épiceries de quartier, connues localement sous le nom de spaza shops, tenues par des ressortissants étrangers.

Des manifestants ont forcé des commerçants étrangers à quitter certains quartiers, tandis que des magasins ont été attaqués et qu'un bâtiment a été incendié, ont rapporté les médias locaux.

La police a indiqué que des renforts avaient été déployés pour prévenir de nouvelles violences.

Les autorités ont promis de poursuivre les responsables de ces destructions.

Ces troubles font suite à une décision rendue en juillet par la Cour constitutionnelle sud-africaine, la plus haute juridiction du pays, qui a invalidé les restrictions empêchant certaines personnes de demander l'asile en raison de leur mode d'entrée sur le territoire ou du non-respect des délais d'immigration.

Ce jugement signifie que les demandeurs d'asile doivent être autorisés à déposer des demandes, même s'ils sont entrés en Afrique du Sud sans les documents requis.

Cette décision a incité des centaines de personnes à se rassembler devant les centres d'accueil des réfugiés, alimentant la colère des militants anti-immigration qui craignent qu'elle n'encourage l'immigration clandestine.

Le porte-parole du gouvernement, William Baloyi, a déclaré à l'agence de presse Reuters que des personnes avaient délibérément répandu de fausses informations concernant le jugement, donnant l'impression que les migrants sans papiers se verraient automatiquement accorder un statut légal.

Baloyi a insisté sur le fait que cette décision n'accorde pas automatiquement aux migrants le statut de réfugié ni le droit de rester de façon permanente en Afrique du Sud.

Les autorités précisent que les demandes continueront d'être évaluées individuellement et que les demandeurs resteront soumis aux contrôles d'immigration.

Plus tôt cette année, des groupes anti-immigration ont organisé des semaines de manifestations exigeant que les ressortissants étrangers sans papiers quittent le pays avant le 30 juin.

Les manifestations ont contraint des dizaines de milliers de migrants à fuir, certains rentrant chez eux grâce à des programmes de rapatriement organisés par leurs gouvernements.

L’Afrique du Sud est confrontée à des attaques xénophobes depuis près de vingt ans. En 2008, plus de 60 personnes ont été tuées et des dizaines de milliers déplacées lors d’attaques généralisées contre des ressortissants étrangers.

Ces troubles surviennent dans un contexte de pauvreté généralisée, de profondes inégalités et de chômage touchant environ un tiers de la population active.

Les migrants sont fréquemment accusés de prendre les emplois, de contribuer à la criminalité et de mettre à rude épreuve les services publics, bien que les chercheurs affirment que ces affirmations catégoriques ne sont étayées par aucune preuve.

Malgré ses difficultés économiques, l'Afrique du Sud demeure l'une des principales destinations du continent pour les migrants en quête d'emploi, de sécurité et de meilleures perspectives.

#5421. 12 rising musicians advance to ABC Young Performers Awards semifinals

The ABC Young Performers Awards offers instrumentalists like pianist Dillon Chan the opportunity to connect with audiences on a national stage.  (Supplied)

After weeks of deliberation, ABC Classic has announced the 12 semifinalists who will progress to the live performance round of the ABC Young Performers Awards in August.

The prestigious competition has launched the careers of some of the most successful Australian musicians, including composer and violist Brett Dean, percussionist Claire Edwardes, violinist Emily Sun and most recently flautist Eliza Shephard.

The competition is open to solo instrumentalists aged 31 and under.

The youngest semifinalist in 2026 is just 13 years old.

Each applicant submitted a 40-minute performance video for the adjudication panel, including at least one piece of music by an Australian composer.

The semifinalists play a range of instruments, including classical guitarist Connor Whyte. (Supplied)

"We were impressed with the overall level of skill, talent, musicality and commitment from all applicants and the energy they brought to this important competition," says Marshall McGuire, the chair of the adjudication panel.

"Competitors who stood out to the panel were bold and imaginative and had a range of repertoire which allowed them to present a full palette of [musical] styles."

The 12 semifinalists represent a wide range of instruments, including piano, violin, cello, flute, saxophone, guitar and percussion, and come from across NSW, Victoria, the ACT and Tasmania.

They will each perform a live public solo recital in Sydney or Melbourne in August.

For many of the competitors, the ABC Young Performers Awards offers a rare national platform, with musicians competing for a variety of reasons.

Pianist Dillon Chan, 13, says performing is about connection rather than competition.

"After some performances, people have come up to me and told me they were really moved, and a few of them have even come back to hear me play again," he says.

For saxophonist Alice Morgan from Sydney, it's a chance to showcase both her instrument and the Australian music she champions.

Saxophonist Alice Morgan is one of 12 semifinalists who will present a recital in the live performance round of the competition. (Supplied)

Morgan has collaborated with composers including Andrew Howes and Holly Harrison, who have written music "with me as the performer in mind."

Classical guitarist Connor Whyte from ACT is hoping to record his first album, while Beatrice Colombis and cellist Charlotte Miles are already forging international careers in Australia and Europe.

Only three finalists will get the chance to compete for a cash prize, and will appear as soloists with the Sydney Symphony Orchestra in a televised performance at the Sydney Opera House in November.

You can find out more about each semifinalist on the ABC Classic website.

The solo recitals in August are open to the public, so you can support the ABC Young Performers Awards semifinalists directly.

On each day, there will be a recital at 12pm, 2pm, 4pm and 6pm.

Tickets are $10 per recital via the ABC Classic website.

If you can't make it in person, recitals will be broadcast on ABC Classic later in the year.

The Grand Final performance will take place on November 3 at the Sydney Opera House Concert Hall, with each of the three grand finalists performing a concerto with the Sydney Symphony Orchestra. The concert will also be broadcast on ABC TV and ABC Classic.

#5423. Agency spends $4 million on redundancies while increasing its spend on contractors

Services Australia nearly doubled the amount it paid out for staff exits in the past financial year as the mega-agency juggled workforce realignments and a costly overhaul of its legacy telecommunications setup.

The agency spent $4.4 million in voluntary redundancy payouts to 28 staff, a jump from just five in 2024-25. On average, $157,000 was paid out per departing employee.

"In 2025-26 voluntary redundancies were used selectively as part of normal workforce management where workforce realignment was required and suitable redeployment was not available," a Services Australia spokesperson said.

The spokesperson said the low redundancy figures in 2024-25 were a result of heavy recruitment in frontline service delivery and the departures in 2025-26 aligned more closely to historical averages of 20 in 2022-23 and 33 in 2023-24.

The agency also forked out about $302 million in communications costs, an increase of $53 million compared with 2024-25.

The spokesperson attributed the increase in spending to rising supplier costs because supply chain inflation across postage and freight in addition to a move away from its legacy telecommunications platforms to a modern digital network.

External legal and contractor spending also increased, driven by what the spokesperson said was a "higher demand for specialist legal advice and support on complex matters".

An overhaul expected of ageing legacy systems is also expected soon so lawyers and contractors can expect to be extremely busy.

In the aftermath of a scathing audit of its cyber security processes, the Department of Parliamentary Services (DPS) has opened its cheque book.

The department awarded contracts worth $5.1 million and $2.38 million to software companies A23 and Informatech for "augmentation resources" for external information technology (IT) contractors.

External specialists were brought in after the Auditor-General found DPS's networks were outdated and vulnerable to attacks, with more than half the staff in the department's cyber security branch having been in their roles for less than a year.

"DPS takes the security, stability and functionality of the Parliamentary Computing Network seriously," a spokesperson said.

"We take a robust and strategic approach to the way we deploy resources to ensure we provide an IT system that meets the needs of the Australian Parliament and the Parliamentary Departments."

On the government's push to reduce contractor reliance, DPS said the splurge was necessary as the technical expertise was "not held within the department and/or may only be required for a short period of time."

For parliamentarians, staffers and press gallery folk hoping for answers about whether the multimillion-dollar contracts would address ongoing Wi-Fi and ParlView issues, DPS did not address network performance citing security protocols.

Parking fines in the Parliamentary Triangle hit $1.6 million last financial year, the National Capital Authority's annual report reveals.

Tickets and fines combined generated about $21 million in non-taxation revenue for the NCA, the statutory authority that collects revenue for the federal government (which theoretically gives it back to Canberrans through the Commonwealth Grants Commission).

But the NCA is still chasing a big chunk of fines owed - $782,000, to be exact.

For those drivers hoping to ignore their unpaid parking fines, the authority warned it would refer them to the ACT Magistrates Court for prosecution.

Nerds in Defence have been sent to drama school in a bid to improve their presentation style, a tender notice has revealed.

The department awarded a $25,300 contract to the National Institute of Dramatic Art (NIDA) which, it turns out, was for 20 bureaucrats in its finance team to brush up on their public speaking.

The lucky group took part in NIDA's Presenting with Confidence course, as part of a joint pilot program with the Australian Taxation Office for developing future finance leaders.

Bean counters were sent to the course to improve their delivery of technical financial data and strategic information to senior executives.

"NIDA was selected for its specialised expertise in executive communication and leadership development," the spokesperson said, adding the course was part of a broader professional development pathway across the APS.

If you're looking forward to your annual wall planner from the Bureau of Meteorology (BOM), it's been sent to the printers.

Public Eye inquired about a $106,126 tender BOM awarded to recruitment agency Ignite Limited.

A spokesperson said the contract was for a small customer service team to handle order processing, payment management and customer inquiries for the 43rd edition of the bureau's official calendar, which will feature amateur and professional photographs selected through a competition.

About 45,000 calendars are printed for sale each year, with an extra 4500 gifted to volunteer weather observers.

If one needed evidence that online scammers were becoming bolder, they should look no further than the website of Australia's corporate regulator.

The Australian Securities and Investments Commission's (ASIC) 2025-26 annual report shows it had to coordinate a takedown of a fake version of its own register portal, ASIC Connect.

The copycat site was part of a complex network linked to a fake trading platform called "Universal Group", which had links impersonating three overseas financial regulators to lend the air of authenticity.

It was just one instance of the exploding game of scam whack-a-mole. For the 2025-26 period, ASIC reported removing 19,400 investment scam and phishing sites, a massive 182 per cent surge from 2024-25.

Scammers were leveraging artificial intelligence and slick web designs to impersonate trusted brands. About 20 per cent of all Moneysmart investor alerts involved fake versions of ASIC-licensed businesses or registered companies.

To help consumers identify fake copycat sites, the regulator has begun publishing official website addresses directly on its Professional Registers Search.

Annual scam losses in Australia had hit $2.2 billion, the report said.

#5425. ‘Clearly disinformation’: Singapore embassy denies claims Indonesian public figures met ambassador

Social media posts had alleged that former Indonesian deputy foreign minister Dino Patti Djalal and political science professor Saiful Mujani met Singapore ambassador Kwok Fook Seng at his residence on Oct 18.

The exterior of Singapore's Embassy in Jakarta. (Photo: Facebook/Singapore Embassy in Jakarta)

SINGAPORE: The Singapore Embassy in Jakarta on Sunday (Oct 25) rejected as disinformation claims that two prominent Indonesian figures met its ambassador, amid heightened online commentary over Indonesia-Singapore relations in recent weeks.

Social media posts had alleged that former deputy foreign minister Dino Patti Djalal and political science professor Saiful Mujani - described in the posts as anti-government figures - met Singapore ambassador Kwok Fook Seng at his residence on Oct 18.

The claims emerged after Dino publicly defended Singapore against allegations that it was conspiring against Indonesia’s interests, including its stock market.

“The Embassy is aware of social media posts containing false statements claiming that Professor Saiful Mujani and Dr Dino Patti Djalal had visited the residence of the Ambassador of Singapore to Indonesia on 18 October 2026,” it said in a statement.

The embassy described the claims as “clearly disinformation” and said it would work with Indonesia’s Ministry of Communication and Digital Affairs to address the issue.

Both Saiful and Dino have also denied the allegations.

Saiful is a professor of political science at Syarif Hidayatullah State Islamic University and founder of Saiful Mujani Research and Consulting.

Dino was Indonesia's deputy minister for foreign affairs in 2014 and has also served as ambassador to the United States. He currently heads the think tank Foreign Policy Community of Indonesia.

CNA Games Guess Word Crack the word, one row at a time Buzzword Create words using the given letters Mini Sudoku Tiny puzzle, mighty brain teaser Mini Crossword Small grid, big challenge Word Search Spot as many words as you can Show More Show Less

According to Indonesian news outlet Kompas, the allegations surfaced after a video purportedly showing the entrance of the Singapore Embassy in Jakarta circulated on social media, accompanied by claims that the two men had met Kwok.

Indonesia’s ruling party Gerindra has also said it was looking into the allegations and the accuracy of the information circulating online.

“The Gerindra Party has been monitoring information that has recently circulated on social media regarding an alleged meeting of anti-government figures with the Singapore Ambassador to Indonesia,” said Bambang Haryadi, secretary of the party’s faction in the House of Representatives, in a statement quoted by state news agency Antara.

Dino described the allegations as “fabricated” and said he would raise the matter with the Indonesia’s Communications and Digital Affairs Minister Meutya Hafid.

"The post began circulating after I made a statement about Indonesia-Singapore relations. Since many people have asked me about this, I want to clarify that the story is 100 per cent fictitious, totally fabricated,” he said in a video posted on Instagram on Sunday.

Dino said he had been in Perth, Australia on Oct 18 to speak at a climate change event and only returned to Indonesia on the evening of Oct 20.

He said he knew Kwok, who has been Singapore’s ambassador to Indonesia since 2022, but had never visited his residence in Jakarta.

Saiful separately said he had never met or spoken to either Dino or Kwok.

“I have never spoken to Mr Dino Patti Djalal, either directly or indirectly, let alone met him. I have also never spoken to the Singapore ambassador to Indonesia, much less met him in person anywhere,” Saiful told Metro TV.

“I am very surprised that the lie claiming I met both of them has gone viral,” he added.

The allegations come amid remarks by current and former Indonesian political figures involving neighbouring countries, including Singapore and Malaysia, as transboundary haze from forest and land fires affected the region.

Dino in a video last week described Singapore as a country with “goodwill, trust and a proven track record of cooperation with Indonesia”.

His comments followed allegations by former Indonesian trade minister Muhammad Lutfi that Singapore state investors Temasek and GIC had sought to pressure global index provider MSCI into downgrading Indonesia’s stock market.

Without naming Lufti, Dino said that any claim that Singapore was conspiring against Indonesia’s equity market “doesn’t make sense”, pointing to Singapore’s substantial investments in Indonesia and assistance during crises including natural disasters and COVID-19.

“Singapore has a vital interest in Indonesia’s political and economic stability because it is one of the countries most affected whenever political and economic turmoil occurs in our country," Dino said.

#5426. Volodymyr Zelenskyy forced to rule out elections as he faces an enemy from within

SBS acknowledges the Traditional Custodians of Country and their connections and continuous care for the skies, lands and waterways throughout Australia.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says it would be too dangerous for Ukraine to hold an election while fighting Russia, after a call by his former defence minister to organise a vote.

As he fended off the political pressure, Zelenskyy announced a new drone deal with Norway, as European leaders arrived for talks ahead of a meeting on Monday to discuss how to pressure Russia to end its invasion.

Ukraine has suspended elections under martial law, a measure still widely supported by the population as the country focuses on fighting off the Russian invasion launched in 2022.

The Ukrainian leader has previously faced calls both from Russian President Vladimir Putin and United States President Donald Trump to stage a vote, even as Russia rains down missiles and drones across the country on a daily basis.

"I believe that in a war like this, elections as such are a huge risk," Zelenskyy said during a briefing with journalists on Saturday.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"Elections right now are a tsunami for the country that will split Ukraine.

"If we want to destroy the country, then we can move in the direction of elections during these times of war," he added.

Ukraine has been engulfed in a political crisis over the summer, triggered when Zelenskyy fired popular defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov. The row forced Zelenskyy to sack his commander-in-chief.

Thousands took to the streets to demand his reinstatement, while Fedorov issued blistering attacks against the army's top brass.

Then, days ago, the ousted Fedorov made a surprise call to find a way to organise elections.

While he did not explicitly state that he wanted to challenge Zelenskyy, the shock move made even some of his supporters distance themselves.

Experts have cited a flurry of obstacles to staging elections.

They include how soldiers, millions of Ukrainian refugees and people from occupied territories would cast their ballots, as well as the threat of both interference and physical attacks from Russia.

Only 15 per cent of Ukrainians believe elections should be held before the end of hostilities, according to an opinion poll.

Zelenskyy, despite facing growing domestic criticism as the war drags on, remains largely popular.

Fedorov's team confirmed to Agence France-Presse on Sunday that he plans to visit the US soon — a trip likely to revive speculation about whether he is positioning himself as a rival to Zelenskyy.

The former minister was a prominent backer of the drone warfare strategy that has come to dominate Ukraine's war with Russia, and had pushed for army reforms — winning support among the public.

On Sunday, several European leaders met Zelenskyy in Kyiv for a Nordic-Baltic summit.

Following individual meetings with several leaders, Zelenskyy announced a drone deal with Norway "that strengthens cooperation between our defence sectors".

Norway's Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre told reporters his country had pledged 85 billion Norwegian krone ($12.5 billion) to Ukraine for next year.

On Monday, Ukraine's independence day, the country's key European backers will meet to discuss Ukraine's current military problems.

Russia has intensified its strikes, using hard-to-intercept ballistic missiles that expose Ukraine's air-defence shortfall.

Ukraine, for its part, has accelerated its own campaign of long-range strikes on Russian energy and logistics sites — including oil refineries and retail warehouses.

On Sunday it hit a warehouse belonging to Russian e-commerce giant Ozon for the second day running.

Zelenskyy said deliveries of crucial interceptor missiles for US Patriot air-defence systems — which can shoot down Russia's ballistic missiles — had halved since 2023.

The US faces its own shortfall of the missiles amid its war on Iran and has been resistant to releasing large numbers to Ukraine.

Civilian deaths in the four-and-a-half-year-long war have surged to their highest since the first months of the invasion amid the uptick in Russian strikes, according to verified statistics from the United Nations.
